speaker: curtisvandeveld
text: The court found that as to that aspect, that the contract required Pacific K and C or required Zongyi to transfer the title to the intended buyer under their contractual relationship. So that was kind of the, it was a mistake, I think, but it was consistent with the contract in that Pacific K and C relied on the fact that it mandatorily was entitled to purchase the title to the lot for the $110,000 and that's in the findings of facts. And so maybe it was not-

speaker: roberttorres
text: What about the HPR issue? I mean, she knew at the time she entered into the contract that that was not going to allow her to convey the title.

speaker: curtisvandeveld
text: Well, that was my argument is to say that was something which Zongyi continuously represented. They were in the process of clearing the HPR problem. And she had put Mr. Harper on notice about the defect by the fact of the findings that there was not commercial financing available and by the provision of the contract that required him to obtain a preliminary title report and to exercise any rights of rescission based upon that. So I think that the circumstances are that there should be a redetermination of this issue. If the court is going to reject the contribution based upon a finding of intentional willful or wanton behavior on the part of Pacific K and C and thereby men, I think that should have been a finding included within the findings of facts and conclusions of law. Otherwise, I think that the provision of 24602B is, and A is in favor of my client in that the trial court should have made a finding to the extent of which each party was at fault relative to the ultimate failure to be able to consummate the contract, which I think is also a part of the fraud in the inducement aspect. And so I believe that the appropriate requirement would have been for the trial court to make the determination. I also think that the-

speaker: roberttorres
text: That'll be a discussion if we're able to get over the hurdle as pointed out by Mr. Mann, that you did not object to the imposition of alternative liability down below. And in fact, at the onset, it was raised in Harper's brief at the beginning and that he suggested you didn't state to the trial court the grounds for that objection on the imposition of alternative liability.

speaker: curtisvandeveld
text: As I said earlier, I believe that the claim for indemnification was the objection to the alternative, the alternative judgment process and that my client preserved that right by making the indemnity claim.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: But Mr. Vanderbilt, just- Yes, Your Honor. Assuming that your client waived the argument, did not preserve the argument, we also have a body of case law that provides for an exception under extraordinary circumstances in which in reference to just exceptional cases that will allow us to, even despite the absence of preserving the issue, why is this, why should we exercise our discretion in this case that makes it an extraordinary case to allow the argument to proceed?

speaker: curtisvandeveld
text: I believe that the issue here presented about whether or not there should be contribution is something I have not been able to find any case law on this in Guam. The issue about the extent to which parties are at fault in contribution is an extremely important aspect of the civil law. And I believe that the court, if it finds that it has not been properly preserved, should because of the importance of this issue and for future cases, I believe that the court should exercise its jurisdiction.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: I mean, the standard is extraordinary circumstances where review is necessary to address a miscarriage of justice or clarify significant issues of law. I don't recall that this is an issue that has come up many times or even a few times in reference to alternative liability versus joining several in the undisclosed principle circumstance. And so it's hard for me to see how we exercise our discretion in very limited circumstances should we agree that your client did not preserve the argument at the trial level.

speaker: curtisvandeveld
text: I believe that even though this has not arisen in the approximately 27 years of the existence of the Supreme Court of Guam, the issue still is important because of the fact that while it may not arise in cases presented to the court, it relates to an extremely important legal issue upon which parties will make decisions whether or not to resolve their respective liabilities amongst one another. And I believe that the fact that it fails to have come to your attention doesn't mean that it doesn't have a significant impact upon the events occurring as between parties relative to civil litigation that may be presented at the trial court level. And so I believe it is a significant legal issue and should fall within the court's extraordinary relief. I also wanted to comment on that the issue of the fraud as reflected by Mr. Mann, that it's strictly somehow fraud on my client's part. The ultimate problem here was based upon the fact that the HPR, the horizontal property regime was a matter which was exclusively within the knowledge of Zhongyi at the time that it made the contract arrangements with my client and sent my client forward to solicit and obtain purchasers. And then persistently representing that it was in the process of clearing that HPR. And to say that somehow it is not substantially responsible for what ultimately did not occur or was able to be completed based upon the relationship with Mr. Harper really lies at the foot of Zhongyi. So I believe that... I'm sorry.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: I will let you finish your sentence, Mr. Vanderbilt. I know that your time is up, but please finish the remaining part of your sentence.

speaker: curtisvandeveld
text: Thank you. Really lies at the foot of Zhongyi. And so if they escape responsibility, it induces people within the community to simply avoid responsibility by having an agent that they tasked to do their bidding, which they, at that time that they're tasking them for that responsibility, know they have no intention of completing. Because the ultimate authority to clear the HPR problem was not with Pacific KNC. It was not within the purview of Min. It was exclusively the province of Zhongyi. Thank you.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderbilt. Thank you. Council, so we want to thank you for your time. There are some novel issues in this case. And at this time, we will take the matter under advisement, issue a written opinion at a later date. And at this time, the court stands adjourned.

speaker: curtisvandeveld
text: Thank you all.

speaker: roberttorres
text: Thank you. Thank you, council.
